messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands: a few folks asked me to post the unanswered comp/leveling items here so we can get written answers. TL;DR: where to find the rules, how exceptions work, and how appeals are handled.
maria: Thanks @alex — will do. I'll post the checklist and short answers, then open to questions.
jamal: Appreciate it. two engineering-specific Qs: 1) if someone gets a tech promotion between cycles, does their manager need to re-run calibration for team impact? 2) how does that affect bonus %?
emily: Also: what's the timeline for off-cycle promotions — do title changes hit payroll immediately or next month?
hr-bot: Autofetching policy links... <https://company-notion/people-ops/comp-cycles|Compensation cycles doc> · <https://company-notion/people-ops/promo-exceptions|Promotion exceptions>
maria: Okay short answers: 1) Off-cycle promotions: managers submit the promo request form (linked). People Ops reviews, if approved we update title and comp. Payroll update usually in the next payroll run (can be same month if cutoff not passed). 2) Bonus impact: off-cycle promos do not retroactively increase prior-cycle bonus % — they affect future bonuses and OTE.
jamal: Got it. For (1) — do we need a new calibration slot, or is manager justification enough?
maria: Manager justification + peer manager signoff is usually fine. We reserve a calibration addendum for promos that are >2 bands or high-dollar adjustments. If it's a standard IC->Senior IC move, the normal approval path suffices.
emily: If someone is promoted but manager forgot to attach calibration notes, can we add them retroactively for audit?
maria: Yes. Add the notes to the HR ticket. We'll attach them to the case before final payroll.
jordan: What about appeals? Someone disagrees with leveling outcome — what's the formal path and timeline?
maria: Appeals path: 1) Team-level discussion -> 2) Manager submits appeal form within 30 days of notice -> 3) People Ops runs an expedited review (30 days target). Escalation to compensation committee if needed. We'll log outcomes in the ticket.
emily: Is there any chance of retroactive comp if an appeal succeeds? Folks worried about lost bonus for the period they were underleveled.
maria: Rare but possible. If the committee finds a material mis-leveling that affected bonus calculations, we can do an ad-hoc adjustment. We evaluate case-by-case and document the rationale.
alex: A few follow-ups from managers: can you share a short checklist of what to include in a strong promo packet?
maria: Yep — paste below (also in Notion):
```
Promo packet checklist:
- Clear impact summary (quantitative where possible)
- Key examples mapped to band rubric sections
- Peer manager signoff (1-2 peers)
- Calibration notes (if available)
- Proposed comp (range + justification)
- Proposed effective date
- Any regulatory/visibility constraints (customer PII, legal review)
```
jamal: Nice. Would love a one-pager for managers we can share in team docs.
maria: Will publish a manager-facing template by EOW.
hr-bot: Notion page created: <https://company-notion/people-ops/promo-template|Promo packet template> :sparkles:
emily: Quick ask — how are band ranges calibrated for SF vs remote cost-of-living? Is there a delta table we can reference?
maria: We use market bands with location differentials for cost-of-living. There's a simple lookup table in the comp doc. If someone is relocating, submit a location change form and comp team will re-run band placement.
jordan: One edge case — contractor -> full-time conversion mid-cycle: how does that affect comp and promo eligibility?
maria: Contractor conversions are handled as new hires for comp purpose. We do consider prior tenure and performance for leveling but bonus eligibility depends on conversion date relative to payroll and bonus windows. We'll triage on a per-case basis.
emily: Thanks — this helps. Any guidance on communicating denials to folks? Managers ask for wording examples.
maria: Use the 'transparent feedback' template in the manager guide. Short example: "Thanks for the great work. After calibration, we didn't approve a promotion this cycle because X and Y. Here's a concrete plan + milestones to help you get there by the next cycle." We'll add a canned script to the template.
alex: Perfect. last ask — who owns tracking of outstanding promo requests so we don't lose anything in Slack?
maria: People Ops owns the ticket until closed. Managers should CC People Ops on ad-hoc notes. I'll set up a weekly digest for pending promos and appeals (starting next Monday).
jamal: Awesome — thanks @maria. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks everyone! ping me any case numbers and I'll add them to the digest.
hr-bot: Event: weekly-promo-digest created. Subscribers: managers, people-ops.
alex: Closing — will copy these answers into the all-hands follow-up doc and share the Notion links. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :white_check_mark:
